subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Matcha: Whisked From Stone
description: A quick win: understand Matcha: Whisked From Stone.

hook.text: Matcha is green tea ground to a powder so fine that you drink the entire leaf—not just an infusion of it.

buildup.text: Shade-grown leaves are steamed, dried, and laboriously ground on granite stone mills. One hour yields just 30 grams.

discovery.text: Because you consume the whole leaf, matcha delivers far more catechins, caffeine, and L-theanine than steeped tea.

twist.text: Ceremonial matcha costs $30–100 per 30 grams. Culinary grade (for lattes) is cheaper but far less nuanced in flavor.

climax.text: The global matcha craze turned a sacred Japanese ritual into a $4 billion industry. Tradition meets commerce.

punchline.text: Not steeped—consumed. One leaf, ground to dust, whisked to froth.

quiz.question: Why is matcha more potent than regular green tea?
options: You consume the entire powdered leaf instead of just an infusion
